prompt:
Research the officially documented limits of AWS Lambda: maximum timeout, maximum memory, and the monthly free tier. Cite AWS's own documentation and quote the limits.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the provided search results, here are the officially documented limits for AWS Lambda regarding maximum timeout, maximum memory, and the monthly free tier.

SOURCE: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/gettingstarted-limits.html | QUOTE: "Function timeout | 900 seconds (15 minutes). For functions using AWS Lambda Managed Instances, asynchronous invocations and event source mapping invocations (except Amazon MQ and Amazon DocumentDB) support a maximum allowed value of 5,400 seconds (90 minutes)." | CLAIM: The maximum timeout for a standard AWS Lambda function is 900 seconds (15 minutes), though certain Managed Instance configurations allow up to 5,400 seconds (90 minutes).

SOURCE: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/gettingstarted-limits.html | QUOTE: "Function memory allocation | 128 MB to 10,240 MB, in 1-MB increments." | CLAIM: The maximum memory allocation for an AWS Lambda function is 10,240 MB.

SOURCE: https://aws.amazon.com/lambda/pricing/ | QUOTE: "The free tier includes one million requests and 400,000 GB-seconds per month." | CLAIM: The AWS Lambda monthly free tier includes 1 million requests and 400,000 GB-seconds of compute duration.
